records.literal_gloss: These [are] the words which spoke Moses to all Israel across the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah, opposite Suph, between Paran and between Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth and Di-zahab.

en.L: These [are] the words that Moses spoke to all Israel across the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel and Laban and Hazeroth and Di-zahab.
en.B: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel in the wilderness across the Jordan: in the Arabah facing Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth and Di-zahab.
en.R: These are the words that Moses spoke to all the people of Israel across the Jordan River. They were in the wilderness, in the Arabah, the low valley, near Suph. The place was between Paran and the places called Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth and Di-zahab.

es.L: Estas [son] las palabras que habló Moisés a todo Israel al otro lado del Jordán, en el desierto, en el Arabá, frente a Suf, entre Parán y Tofel y Labán y Hazerot y Dizahab.
es.B: Estas son las palabras que Moisés dirigió a todo Israel en el desierto, al otro lado del Jordán: en el Arabá, frente a Suf, entre Parán y Tofel, Labán, Hazerot y Dizahab.
es.R: Estas son las palabras que Moisés le dijo a todo el pueblo de Israel al otro lado del río Jordán. Estaban en el desierto, en el Arabá, el gran valle profundo, cerca de Suf. El lugar quedaba entre Parán y los sitios llamados Tofel, Labán, Hazerot y Dizahab.

fr.L: Ce [sont] les paroles que Moïse dit à tout Israël au-delà du Jourdain, dans le désert, dans l’Araba, en face de Souph, entre Parân et Tophel et Laban et Hatséroth et Di-Zahab.
fr.B: Voici les paroles que Moïse adressa à tout Israël dans le désert, au-delà du Jourdain : dans l’Araba, face à Souph, entre Parân et Tophel, Laban, Hatséroth et Di-Zahab.
fr.R: Voici les paroles que Moïse a dites à tout le peuple d’Israël, de l’autre côté du fleuve Jourdain. Ils étaient dans le désert, dans l’Araba, la grande vallée profonde, près de Souph. L’endroit se trouvait entre Parân et les lieux appelés Tophel, Laban, Hatséroth et Di-Zahab.

sw.L: Haya [ndiyo] maneno ambayo Musa aliwaambia Israeli wote ng'ambo ya Yordani, nyikani, katika Araba, mkabala na Sufu, kati ya Parani na Tofeli na Labani na Haserothi na Di-zahabu.
sw.B: Haya ndiyo maneno ambayo Musa aliwaambia Israeli wote nyikani ng'ambo ya Yordani: katika Araba, mkabala na Sufu, kati ya Parani na Tofeli, Labani, Haserothi na Di-zahabu.
sw.R: Haya ndiyo maneno ambayo Musa aliwaambia watu wote wa Israeli ng'ambo ya Mto Yordani. Walikuwa jangwani, katika Araba, yaani bonde kubwa lenye kina, karibu na Sufu. Mahali hapo palikuwa kati ya Parani na sehemu zinazoitwa Tofeli, Labani, Haserothi na Di-zahabu.

ko.L: 이것은 모세가 요단 건너편 광야에서, 곧 숩 맞은편 아라바에서, 바란과 도벨과 라반과 하세롯과 디사합 사이에서 온 이스라엘에게 한 말들이다.
ko.B: 이것은 모세가 요단강 건너편 광야에서 온 이스라엘에게 한 말이다. 그곳은 숩 맞은편 아라바로, 바란과 도벨, 라반, 하세롯, 디사합 사이였다.
ko.R: 이것은 모세가 요단강 건너편에서 온 이스라엘 백성에게 한 말이다. 그때 그들은 광야에, 곧 낮은 골짜기인 아라바에 있었고, 숩과 가까운 곳이었다. 그곳은 바란과, 도벨, 라반, 하세롯, 디사합이라는 곳들 사이에 있었다.

vi.L: Đây [là] những lời mà Môi-se đã nói với cả Y-sơ-ra-ên ở bên kia sông Giô-đanh, trong hoang mạc, trong A-ra-ba, đối diện Su-phơ, giữa Pha-ran và Tô-phên, La-ban, Hát-sê-rốt và Đi-xa-háp.
vi.B: Đây là những lời Môi-se đã nói với toàn thể Y-sơ-ra-ên trong hoang mạc, bên kia sông Giô-đanh: tại A-ra-ba, đối diện Su-phơ, giữa Pha-ran và Tô-phên, La-ban, Hát-sê-rốt và Đi-xa-háp.
vi.R: Đây là những lời Môi-se đã nói với toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên ở bên kia sông Giô-đanh. Lúc ấy họ đang ở trong hoang mạc, tại A-ra-ba, là thung lũng thấp, gần Su-phơ. Nơi ấy nằm giữa Pha-ran và những nơi gọi là Tô-phên, La-ban, Hát-sê-rốt và Đi-xa-háp.

decisions.choice: These are the words: the opening of Moses' farewell speeches, given in Moab, across the Jordan, in the fortieth year
decisions.reason: The book begins by naming what it holds: words that Moses spoke to the whole people. Verses 3-5 then fix the time and place. It is the fortieth year after the departure from Egypt (verse 3), after the victories over Sihon and Og (verse 4), and Israel is camped in the land of Moab, east of the Jordan (verse 5), on the edge of the land that Moses himself will not enter (verse 37; 34:1-5). Most of the book is Moses speaking; the narrator's own voice is heard only in a few places (1:1-5; 4:41-49; 5:1; and parts of chapters 27-34). The Hebrew name of the book, "Words", comes from this opening line.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: the region east of the river, named from the viewpoint of the land to the west
decisions.reason: The phrase means "on the other side of the Jordan". Here it is the land east of the river, where Israel was camped in the plains of Moab (verse 5; Numbers 22:1). It is named as seen from the land west of the Jordan, the land of Canaan that God had promised to Israel, so that the east side is "across" the river. The same phrase can point the other way: when Moses, standing in the east, speaks of the land Israel will enter, "across the Jordan" means the west (3:20, 25; 11:30). The phrase names a region; by itself it does not say where the speaker or the writer was standing.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, Suph, Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, Di-zahab: the rift valley and places whose sites are mostly unknown
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the deep valley that runs from the Sea of Galilee south through the Jordan and the Dead Sea to the gulf at Elath; here it is the part of it in Moab, opposite Jericho (Numbers 22:1). Paran is the wilderness south of Canaan (Numbers 10:12; 13:26), and Hazeroth was a camp on the way from Sinai (Numbers 11:35; 33:17). Suph, Tophel, Laban and Di-zahab cannot be located today; Suph may be connected with the name of the Sea of Reeds. The list may describe the region where Moses spoke, or it may recall places on the journey from Horeb; the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, the low valley
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the name and adds a short description, because "Arabah" means nothing to most readers. It also adds "River" to "the Jordan" and breaks the long list of places into short sentences.

decisions.choice: the narrator's frame (1:1-5 and the other narrated passages) in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("dit", "adressa") and the passé composé at Readable ("a dites"); Moses' speeches, which retell the past, in the passé composé (with imparfait and plus-que-parfait) at every level ("nous a parlé", 1:6)
alternatives: passé simple for the events Moses retells at Literal and Balanced
passé composé at every level, the narrator included
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy. The French style guide sets the passé simple for written narrative at Literal and Balanced and the passé composé at Readable. Almost all of Deuteronomy, though, is Moses speaking to the people, and a story told inside speech keeps the tenses of speech, as the speeches of Acts and the parables do: Moses says what "the LORD has done" for the people he is talking to, so the passé composé is used for it at every level. Laws and commands are in the future or present at Literal and Balanced ("tu ne tueras pas") and "tu dois" or the imperative at Readable.

decisions.choice: "nyika" (nyikani) for the wilderness at Literal and Balanced, "jangwa" (jangwani) at Readable
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy, as in Exodus and the New Testament: the midbar is open, dry grazing land rather than sand desert, which "nyika" says; Readable uses "jangwa", the everyday word most readers know.

decisions.choice: "요단 건너편" (Literal) and "요단강 건너편" (Balanced, Readable) for "across the Jordan"; "요단강" written without a space
decisions.reason: Korean keeps the Hebrew viewpoint, the land east of the river seen from the west, as the English does; the meaning decision explains it. "요단강" is spelled as one word, as Joshua already has it, which the Exodus-Deuteronomy drafts settled over the term sheet's "요단 강".

decisions.choice: Narrative in the plain written style (-다, -었다); Moses' speeches in 해라체 with "너희" / "너" at Literal and Balanced and in 합쇼체 with "여러분" at Readable
decisions.reason: As the Exodus-Deuteronomy term sheet sets for Moses speaking to Israel: the plain style of an elder and lawgiver at Literal and Balanced, and a respectful public address at Readable that new readers hear as a sermon. Recorded once for the book; later chapters follow it.

decisions.choice: "nói" for Moses speaking, "phán" for God
decisions.reason: As the Vietnamese style guide sets, "phán" is kept for God speaking and every human speaker, Moses included, "nói". Deuteronomy is almost all Moses' speech; where he reports what God said, the verb is "phán".

decisions.choice: "Su-phơ", "Pha-ran", "Tô-phên", "La-ban", "Hát-sê-rốt", "Đi-xa-háp"
decisions.reason: Names follow the Protestant transliterations: "Pha-ran" and "Hát-sê-rốt" as Genesis 21:21 and Numbers 12:16; the others are spelled in the same way and kept through the book.

source.text: אַחַ֨ד עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ מֵֽחֹרֵ֔ב דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַר־שֵׂעִ֑יר עַ֖ד קָדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: Eleven day[s] from Horeb, [by the] way of mount Seir, to Kadesh-barnea.

en.L: Eleven days [it is] from Horeb, by the way of Mount Seir, to Kadesh-barnea.
en.B: It is eleven days' journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by the Mount Seir road.
en.R: The trip from Horeb, the mountain also called Sinai, to Kadesh-barnea takes eleven days along the road through the hills of Seir.

es.L: Once días [hay] desde Horeb, por el camino del monte Seír, hasta Cades-barnea.
es.B: Desde Horeb hasta Cades-barnea hay once días de camino por la ruta del monte Seír.
es.R: El viaje desde Horeb, el monte que también se llama Sinaí, hasta Cades-barnea dura once días por el camino que atraviesa las colinas de Seír.

fr.L: [Il y a] onze jours depuis l’Horeb, par le chemin de la montagne de Séir, jusqu’à Kadesh-Barnéa.
fr.B: Il faut onze jours pour aller de l’Horeb à Kadesh-Barnéa par la route de la montagne de Séir.
fr.R: De l’Horeb, la montagne qu’on appelle aussi le Sinaï, jusqu’à Kadesh-Barnéa, le voyage dure onze jours par la route qui traverse les collines de Séir.

sw.L: [Ni] siku kumi na moja kutoka Horebu, kwa njia ya mlima Seiri, hadi Kadesh-barnea.
sw.B: Ni safari ya siku kumi na moja kutoka Horebu hadi Kadesh-barnea kwa njia ya Mlima Seiri.
sw.R: Safari kutoka Horebu, mlima unaoitwa pia Sinai, hadi Kadesh-barnea huchukua siku kumi na moja kwa njia inayopita katika vilima vya Seiri.

ko.L: 호렙에서 세일 산 길로 가데스바네아까지는 열하루 [길]이다.
ko.B: 호렙에서 세일 산길을 따라 가데스바네아까지는 열하루 길이다.
ko.R: 시내 산이라고도 하는 호렙 산에서 세일 산지를 지나는 길로 가데스바네아까지 가면 열하루가 걸린다.

vi.L: Từ Hô-rếp, theo đường núi Sê-i-rơ, đến Ca-đe Ba-nê-a [là] mười một ngày [đường].
vi.B: Từ Hô-rếp đến Ca-đe Ba-nê-a theo đường núi Sê-i-rơ là mười một ngày đường.
vi.R: Từ núi Hô-rếp, cũng gọi là núi Si-na-i, đến Ca-đe Ba-nê-a phải đi mất mười một ngày, theo con đường xuyên qua vùng đồi núi Sê-i-rơ.

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain of God, also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Horeb is the mountain where God appeared to Moses in the bush (Exodus 3:1) and where he made his covenant with Israel (4:10, 15; 5:2). Exodus and Numbers usually call it Sinai (Exodus 19:11; Numbers 10:12); Deuteronomy calls it Horeb.

decisions.choice: the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea: the route north through the region of Edom to the oasis on the southern edge of Canaan
decisions.reason: Mount Seir is the hill country of Edom, south of the Dead Sea (2:1, 4-5; Genesis 36:8). Kadesh-barnea, often simply Kadesh, was an oasis at the edge of the wilderness of Paran and Zin, south of the land of Canaan. The spies were sent from there and Israel later camped there (Numbers 13:26; 20:1; 32:8).

decisions.choice: eleven days: a short journey set against the forty years of verse 3
decisions.reason: Placed beside the date in verse 3, the distance makes a point: the way from Horeb to the edge of the land took eleven days, but Israel reached the land only in the fortieth year. Verses 19-46 tell why: at Kadesh the people refused to go in, and that generation wandered until it died out (Numbers 14:33-34).

decisions.choice: Horeb, the mountain also called Sinai
decisions.reason: Readable adds the better known name so that readers recognize the mountain of the Ten Commandments.

decisions.choice: "l'Horeb", with the article ("à l'Horeb", "de l'Horeb")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy, as the Pentateuch terms list: French names mountains with the article, as it says "le Sinaï", so the mountain of God is "l'Horeb". Readable says "le mont Horeb" where the English says "Mount Horeb". Kadesh-barnea is "Kadesh-Barnéa", the French form of the Hebrew name, and "la montagne de Séir" follows Genesis 36.

decisions.choice: "가데스바네아" written as one word
decisions.reason: The place name is spelled as Joshua 10:41 and 15:3 already spell it in Korean.

decisions.choice: "Ca-đe Ba-nê-a"
decisions.reason: The term sheet spells Kadesh "Ca-đe" (as Numbers 20:1); Barnea is added as a second word, as other double names are written ("Ê-xi-ôn Ghê-be"). Joshua 14:6 has "Ca-đê-Ba-nê-a"; a reviewer should make the two agree.

decisions.choice: "Si-na-i"
decisions.reason: The form settled for these books, as Acts 7 and Galatians 4.

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ בְּאַרְבָּעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי־עָשָׂ֥ר חֹ֖דֶשׁ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ דִּבֶּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כְּ֠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֹת֖וֹ אֲלֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in [the] fortieth year, in [the] eleventh month, on [the] first of the month, spoke Moses to [the] sons of Israel according to all that had commanded Yahweh him for them.

en.L: And it was in the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first [day] of the month, [that] Moses spoke to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel according to all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him for them.
en.B: On the first day of the eleventh month, in the fortieth year, Moses spoke to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and told them everything that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him to give them.
en.R: Moses spoke to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} on the first day of the eleventh month, in the fortieth year after they left Egypt. He told them everything that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded him to tell them.

es.L: Y sucedió en el año cuarenta, en el mes undécimo, el [día] primero del mes, [que] Moisés habló a los hijos de Israel conforme a todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había mandado para ellos.
es.B: El primer día del mes undécimo del año cuarenta, Moisés habló a los israelitas y les comunicó todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había mandado darles.
es.R: Moisés habló a los israelitas el primer día del mes once, en el año cuarenta después de que salieron de Egipto. Les dijo todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le había mandado decirles.

fr.L: Et il arriva, la quarantième année, au onzième mois, le premier [jour] du mois, [que] Moïse parla aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël selon tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui avait commandé pour eux.
fr.B: Le premier jour du onzième mois de la quarantième année, Moïse parla aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} et leur transmit tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui avait ordonné de leur donner.
fr.R: Moïse a parlé aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} le premier jour du onzième mois, dans la quarantième année après leur sortie d’Égypte. Il leur a dit tout ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui avait commandé de leur dire.

sw.L: Ikawa katika mwaka wa arobaini, katika mwezi wa kumi na moja, siku ya kwanza ya mwezi, Musa akasema na wana wa Israeli sawasawa na yote ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwamuru kwa ajili yao.
sw.B: Siku ya kwanza ya mwezi wa kumi na moja, katika mwaka wa arobaini, Musa alisema na Waisraeli, akawaambia yote ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwagiza awape.
sw.R: Musa aliongea na Waisraeli siku ya kwanza ya mwezi wa kumi na moja, katika mwaka wa arobaini tangu walipotoka Misri. Aliwaambia kila kitu ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwamuru awaambie.

ko.L: 그리고 사십 년째 되는 해 열한째 달 그달 첫째 [날]에, 모세는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 명령하여 그들에게 [전하게] 하신 모든 것대로 이스라엘 자손에게 말했다.
ko.B: 사십 년째 되는 해 열한째 달 초하루에, 모세는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이스라엘 백성에게 전하라고 자기에게 명령하신 모든 것을 그들에게 말했다.
ko.R: 이집트를 떠난 지 사십 년째 되는 해 열한째 달 첫째 날에, 모세가 이스라엘 사람들에게 말했다. 그는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 전하라고 명령하신 것을 모두 그들에게 알려 주었다.

vi.L: Và [việc xảy ra] vào năm thứ bốn mươi, tháng thứ mười một, ngày mồng một trong tháng, Môi-se nói với con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên theo mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho ông [nói] với họ.
vi.B: Vào ngày mồng một tháng mười một, năm thứ bốn mươi, Môi-se nói với dân Y-sơ-ra-ên mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho ông để truyền lại cho họ.
vi.R: Môi-se nói với dân Y-sơ-ra-ên vào ngày mồng một tháng mười một, năm thứ bốn mươi kể từ khi họ ra khỏi Ai Cập. Ông cho họ biết mọi điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã truyền cho ông phải nói với họ.

decisions.choice: the fortieth year, the eleventh month, the first day: forty years after the departure from Egypt, near the end of that year
decisions.reason: The years are counted from the departure from Egypt, as in Numbers 33:38, where Aaron dies in the fortieth year. The date leaves about two months before the crossing of the Jordan in the first month of the next year (Joshua 4:19), time enough for Moses' speeches, his death, and thirty days of mourning (34:8).

decisions.choice: according to all that the LORD had commanded him: Moses passes on God's own commands
decisions.reason: What Moses is about to say is not his own program. He speaks as the one who received God's words at Horeb and hands them on to the people (5:5, 27-31; 18:18).

decisions.choice: after they left Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says from what point the forty years are counted, which the Hebrew leaves to the reader (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy, as in Genesis and Exodus: the divine name is "el SEÑOR" in small capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", with "Yahvé" as the reader setting. The span takes in the article and any contraction ("del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé"), since "Yahvé" takes no article. "Jehová", the Reina-Valera form, is a later hybrid of the consonants of the name and the vowels of "Adonai"; plain "el Señor" would hide that the name is used. Adonai YHWH is "Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}".

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" (L); "los israelitas" (B, R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in English
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy, as in Exodus: Spanish "hijos" already takes in daughters, so the Literal "los hijos de Israel" is inclusive and needs no setting; Balanced and Readable say "los israelitas", as the English says "Israelites".

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}

decisions.choice: he struck: Moses, as Israel's leader
decisions.reason: The subject is Moses, the last person named (verse 3). The victories belong to Israel under his leadership, and Moses himself will say that it was the LORD who gave these kings into their hands (2:24, 31-36; 3:1-3).

decisions.choice: Sihon and Og: the two kings east of the Jordan whose lands Israel had just taken
decisions.reason: Sihon ruled the land of the Amorites between the Arnon and the Jabbok rivers from his city Heshbon; Og ruled Bashan, the high plain farther north, east of the Sea of Galilee (Numbers 21:21-35). Their defeat gave Israel its first land, later given to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh (3:12-17), and it is often recalled as a sign of what God will do west of the Jordan (2:24-3:11; 31:4).

decisions.choice: in Ashtaroth, in Edrei: Og's two royal cities
alternatives: who lived in Ashtaroth, when he defeated him at Edrei
decisions.reason: Joshua 12:4 and 13:12 say that Og reigned "in Ashtaroth and in Edrei", so the two names here are read as his two cities. The words could also mean that Moses defeated Og at Edrei, where the battle was fought (3:1; Numbers 21:33).

decisions.choice: who ruled from
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the kings "sat" or "dwelt" in these cities. For a king that means the city where he had his throne, so Readable says "ruled from".

decisions.choice: "los amorreos"; "Sijón", "Hesbón", "Og", "Basán", "Astarot", "Edrei"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy: "los amorreos" as in Genesis and the Pentateuch terms list; the kings, cities and regions in their usual Spanish forms.

decisions.choice: "les Amoréens"; "Sihon", "Heshbon", "Og", "le Bashân", "Ashtaroth", "Édréï"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy: "les Amoréens" as in Genesis 15 and the Pentateuch terms list. The other names transcribe the Hebrew as the French of Genesis does, writing "sh" for shin (Heshbon, Ashtaroth); Bashan takes the article, as a region ("le roi du Bashân").

decisions.choice: "Waamori"; "Sihoni", "Heshboni", "Ogu", "Bashani", "Ashtarothi", "Edrei"
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy: "Waamori" as in Genesis and the Pentateuch terms list; the other names follow the Hebrew with the final vowel Swahili writes.

decisions.choice: "đóng đô tại" (B); "cai trị từ" (R)
decisions.reason: "dwelling in" a city, said of a king, is where he reigned (meaning decision on Og's royal cities); "đóng đô" is the word Joshua 12:2-4 uses for the same two kings.

vi.R: Tại đó, bên kia sông Giô-đanh, trong xứ Mô-áp, Môi-se bắt đầu giải thích những lời dạy dỗ này. Ông nói:

decisions.choice: torah, this law: instruction, the whole of what Moses teaches in this book, not only its rules
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to point the way or to teach, and it names instruction, as a parent's teaching is called by this word (Proverbs 1:8; 3:1). "This law" in Deuteronomy is the whole body of Moses' teaching: the story of what God has done for Israel, the call to love him and keep his covenant, and the statutes and rulings that go with it (4:44-45; 17:18-19; 31:9-12). It contains commands, but it is more than a code of laws.

decisions.choice: make clear: explain, set out plainly
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something plain and easy to read. It is used of writing the law "very plainly" on stones (27:8) and of writing a vision plainly on tablets (Habakkuk 2:2). Moses is not giving another law but setting out and explaining God's instruction for the people who are about to enter the land.

decisions.choice: undertook: set himself to the task, began
decisions.reason: The verb means to make up one's mind to do something, to venture on it, as Abraham does when he dares to speak to God (Genesis 18:27). Moses now begins the long task of teaching.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan, in the land of Moab: the plains of Moab opposite Jericho
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, "across the Jordan" is the east side of the river. The place is the plains of Moab across from Jericho, where Israel was camped at the end of Numbers (Numbers 22:1; 36:13), in land that had once been Moab's.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "law". Readable says "teaching", because "law" by itself makes most readers think only of rules, and what follows begins with history and appeal (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "sheria hii" (L, B); "mafundisho haya" (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy: "sheria" follows the English "law" at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says "mafundisho" (teaching), as the English Readable does. "Torati" is familiar as the name of the five books, but here torah is the teaching Moses is giving, not yet a book.

decisions.choice: "율법" for torah at Literal and Balanced; "가르침" at Readable
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "율법" for torah; the meaning decision says it means the whole of Moses' instruction, which Readable makes plain with "가르침", as the English Readable says "teaching".

decisions.choice: "luật pháp" (L, B); "những lời dạy dỗ" (R)
decisions.reason: "luật pháp" is the term sheet's word for torah. The meaning decision says it is the whole of Moses' instruction, not only rules, so Readable says "lời dạy dỗ", as the English Readable says "teaching".

decisions.choice: the LORD our God spoke to us: Moses' first speech begins here and runs to 4:40
decisions.reason: The narrator's introduction (verses 1-5) ends, and Moses speaks. His first speech looks back over the journey from Horeb to Moab (1:6-3:29) and then calls the people to obey (4:1-40). Within it he quotes God, the people and his own earlier words.

decisions.choice: our God ... to us: the generation in Moab spoken of as the people who were at Horeb
decisions.reason: Most of those Moses addresses were children at Horeb or not yet born (verses 35, 39). He still says that God spoke "to us", because Israel is addressed as one people through its generations, and the covenant made at Horeb is theirs too (5:2-3).

decisions.choice: you have stayed at this mountain: the year or so Israel spent at Horeb
decisions.reason: Israel reached the mountain in the third month after leaving Egypt (Exodus 19:1) and left in the second month of the second year (Numbers 10:11-12). There God gave the covenant and the laws and the tabernacle was built. Now it is time to move toward the land.

decisions.choice: long enough
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "much for you", that is, it has been enough. Balanced and Readable say "long enough", because the point is the length of the stay.

decisions.choice: ustedes forms by default ("ustedes", "han estado", "llevan"); vosotros forms with the plural-you setting ("vosotros", "habéis estado", "lleváis")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy, as in Genesis 1:28 and Exodus: wherever several people are addressed, Spanish must choose a plural form of address. The default is the "ustedes" form used by most Spanish speakers; the plural-you setting gives the "vosotros" form of Spain. The span covers each verb, pronoun or possessive phrase that changes ("{{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}}"). Where the Hebrew addresses Israel in the singular, Spanish says "tú" and has no span (see 1:8).

decisions.choice: At Readable Moses speaks to the people in 합쇼체, but God's words that he quotes stay in 해라체 with "너희"
decisions.reason: God speaks in 해라체 throughout the Old Testament drafts; Moses' own address to the people is what becomes formal at Readable, not the words he reports.

decisions.choice: God to Israel: "các ngươi" at every level
decisions.reason: When Moses quotes God speaking to the people, God calls them "các ngươi" at every level, as in the laws of Exodus to Numbers; "anh em" is Moses' own word for them at Balanced and Readable.

en.L: Turn and set out for yourselves, and go into the hill country of the Amorites and to all its neighbors, in the Arabah, in the hill country and in the Shephelah and in the Negev and on the shore of the sea, the land of the Canaanites, and the Lebanon, up to the great river, the river Euphrates.
en.B: Turn and move on. Go into the hill country of the Amorites and to all the regions near it: the Arabah, the hill country, the foothills, the Negev and the seacoast, the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
en.R: Break camp and go on your way. Go into the hill country where the Amorites live and to all the places around it: the Jordan Valley, the hills, the low hills in the west, the southern desert and the seacoast. Go into the land of the Canaanites and into Lebanon, as far as the great Euphrates River.

es.L: {{plural_you:Vuélvanse|Volveos}} y {{plural_you:partan|partid}}, y {{plural_you:entren|entrad}} en la región montañosa de los amorreos y a todos sus vecinos, en el Arabá, en la región montañosa, en la Sefelá, en el Néguev y en la costa del mar, la tierra de los cananeos, y el Líbano, hasta el gran río, el río Éufrates.
es.B: {{plural_you:Pónganse|Poneos}} en marcha y {{plural_you:sigan|seguid}} adelante. {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la región montañosa de los amorreos y a todas las regiones cercanas: el Arabá, la montaña, las estribaciones, el Néguev y la costa del mar, la tierra de los cananeos, y el Líbano, hasta el gran río, el Éufrates.
es.R: {{plural_you:Levanten|Levantad}} el campamento y {{plural_you:sigan su camino|seguid vuestro camino}}. {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a la región de colinas donde viven los amorreos y a todos los lugares que la rodean: el valle del Jordán, las colinas, las colinas bajas del oeste, el desierto del sur y la costa. {{plural_you:Entren|Entrad}} en la tierra de los cananeos y en el Líbano, hasta el gran río Éufrates.

fr.L: Tournez-vous et mettez-vous en route, et allez à la montagne des Amoréens et vers tous ses voisins, dans l’Araba, dans la montagne, dans la Shefela, dans le Néguev et sur le rivage de la mer, le pays des Cananéens, et le Liban, jusqu’au grand fleuve, le fleuve Euphrate.
fr.B: Tournez-vous et reprenez la route. Entrez dans la région montagneuse des Amoréens et dans toutes les contrées voisines : l’Araba, la montagne, le piémont, le Néguev et le littoral, le pays des Cananéens, et le Liban, jusqu’au grand fleuve, l’Euphrate.
fr.R: Levez le camp et remettez-vous en route. Allez dans la région de collines où vivent les Amoréens et dans tous les endroits autour : la vallée du Jourdain, les collines, les basses collines de l’ouest, le désert du sud et la côte de la mer. Allez dans le pays des Cananéens et au Liban, jusqu’au grand fleuve Euphrate.

sw.L: Geukeni na mwondoke, mwende katika nchi ya milima ya Waamori na kwa jirani zake wote, katika Araba, katika nchi ya milima, katika Shefela, katika Negebu na katika pwani ya bahari, nchi ya Wakanaani, na Lebanoni, hadi ule mto mkubwa, mto Frati.
sw.B: Geukeni mwendelee na safari. Nendeni katika nchi ya milima ya Waamori na katika maeneo yote yaliyo jirani nayo: Araba, nchi ya milima, vilima vya chini, Negebu na pwani ya bahari, nchi ya Wakanaani, na Lebanoni, hadi mto mkubwa, Frati.
sw.R: Vunjeni kambi, mwendelee na safari. Nendeni katika nchi ya vilima wanamoishi Waamori na katika sehemu zote zinazoizunguka: bonde la Yordani, vilima, vilima vya chini upande wa magharibi, jangwa la kusini na pwani ya bahari. Nendeni katika nchi ya Wakanaani na Lebanoni, hadi mto mkubwa wa Frati.

ko.L: 너희는 방향을 돌려 길을 떠나, 아모리 사람의 산지로, 그리고 그 이웃한 모든 곳, 곧 아라바와 산지와 세벨라와 네게브와 바닷가, 가나안 사람의 땅과 레바논, 큰 강, 곧 유프라테스강까지 가라.
ko.B: 너희는 발길을 돌려 떠나라. 아모리 사람의 산지로 가고, 그 주변의 모든 지역, 곧 아라바와 산지와 서쪽 구릉 지대와 네게브와 바닷가와 가나안 사람의 땅과 레바논으로, 큰 강 유프라테스까지 가라.
ko.R: 진을 거두고 길을 떠나라. 아모리 사람들이 사는 산지로 가고, 그 둘레의 모든 곳으로 가라. 곧 요단 골짜기와 산지와 서쪽의 낮은 언덕 지대와 남쪽 광야와 바닷가로 가라. 가나안 사람들의 땅과 레바논으로, 큰 강 유프라테스까지 가라.

vi.L: Hãy quay lại và lên đường, đi vào miền đồi núi của người A-mô-rít và đến mọi [vùng] lân cận của nó, trong A-ra-ba, trong miền đồi núi, trong Sơ-phê-la, trong Nê-ghép và trên bờ biển, xứ của người Ca-na-an, và Li-ban, cho đến sông lớn, sông Ơ-phơ-rát.
vi.B: Hãy quay lại và đi tiếp. Hãy vào miền đồi núi của người A-mô-rít và mọi vùng lân cận: A-ra-ba, miền đồi núi, vùng đồi thấp, Nê-ghép và miền duyên hải, tức là xứ của người Ca-na-an, và Li-ban, cho đến sông lớn là sông Ơ-phơ-rát.
vi.R: Hãy nhổ trại và lên đường. Hãy đi vào miền đồi núi nơi người A-mô-rít sống và đến mọi nơi chung quanh đó: thung lũng Giô-đanh, vùng đồi núi, vùng đồi thấp ở phía tây, miền nam khô hạn và miền ven biển. Hãy đi vào xứ của người Ca-na-an và vào Li-ban, cho đến tận sông lớn Ơ-phơ-rát.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, the hill country, the Shephelah, the Negev, the coast: the regions of the land, from east to west and south
decisions.reason: The list names the parts of the land as Israel knew them: the Arabah, the Jordan valley in the east; the central hill country; the Shephelah, the low hills between the hills and the coastal plain; the Negev, the dry south; and the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. Lebanon is the mountain range to the north.

decisions.choice: as far as the great river, the Euphrates: the full extent of the land promised to Abraham
decisions.reason: These are the borders God promised to Abraham (Genesis 15:18), repeated in Exodus 23:31, Deuteronomy 11:24 and Joshua 1:4. They mark the whole of the promise, wider than the land Israel would hold in Joshua's day.

decisions.choice: Amorites, Canaanites: names for the peoples living in the land
decisions.reason: "Amorites" here means the peoples of the hill country of Canaan in general (verses 19-20, 27, 44; Genesis 15:16), and "Canaanites" those of the lowlands and coast (Numbers 13:29). Both names can stand for all the inhabitants of the land.

decisions.choice: Break camp and go on your way
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "turn and set out". Readable uses the plain words for leaving a camp. Readable also describes the regions instead of naming them ("the low hills in the west" for the Shephelah, "the southern desert" for the Negev).

decisions.choice: "la Shefela" (L), "le piémont" (B); "le Néguev"; "les Cananéens"; "le Liban"
alternatives: "la plaine" or "le bas-pays" for the Shephelah
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the region's Hebrew name, as the English does; Balanced says what it is, the low hills at the foot of the hill country, as the English "foothills". "Les Cananéens" and "le Néguev" as in Genesis and the Pentateuch terms list.

decisions.choice: "서쪽 구릉 지대" (Balanced) and "서쪽의 낮은 언덕 지대" (Readable) for the Shephelah; "네게브" kept as a name at Balanced, "남쪽 광야" at Readable
decisions.reason: As Joshua has it in Korean: Literal keeps the name "세벨라", the other levels describe the low hills between the mountains and the coast.

decisions.choice: "Sơ-phê-la" (L); "vùng đồi thấp" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the region's name, as 1 Kings 10:27; Balanced and Readable describe it, as Joshua 11:16 does ("vùng đồi thấp").

records.literal_gloss: See, I have set before you the land; go in and take possession of the land which swore Yahweh to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them and to their offspring after them.

en.L: See, I have set before you the land. Go in and take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, that [he would] give [it] to them and to their offspring after them.'
en.B: Look, I have placed the land in front of you. Go in and take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to give to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and to their descendants after them.'
en.R: Look, the land is in front of you, and I am giving it to you. Go in and take it as your own. I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, made a promise with an oath to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. I promised to give this land to them and to their descendants after them.'

es.L: Mira, he puesto delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} la tierra; {{plural_you:entren|entrad}} y {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} posesión de la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} juró a {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}}, a Abraham, a Isaac y a Jacob, que [la] daría a ellos y a su descendencia después de ellos.”
es.B: Mira, he puesto la tierra delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Entren|Entrad}} y {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} posesión de la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} juró dar a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} Abraham, Isaac y Jacob, y a sus descendientes después de ellos.”
es.R: Mira, la tierra está delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y yo {{plural_you:se la doy|os la doy}}. {{plural_you:Entren y tómenla como suya|Entrad y tomadla como vuestra}}. Yo, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, les hice una promesa con juramento a {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} Abraham, Isaac y Jacob. Prometí darles esta tierra a ellos y a sus descendientes después de ellos.”

fr.L: Vois, j’ai mis devant vous le pays ; entrez et prenez possession du pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a juré à vos pères, à Abraham, à Isaac et à Jacob, de leur donner, à eux et à leur descendance après eux.”
fr.B: Regarde : j’ai placé le pays devant vous. Entrez et prenez possession du pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a juré de donner à vos ancêtres Abraham, Isaac et Jacob, ainsi qu’à leurs descendants après eux.”
fr.R: Regarde, le pays est devant vous, et je vous le donne. Entrez-y et prenez-le, il sera à vous. Moi, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, j’ai fait une promesse avec serment à vos ancêtres Abraham, Isaac et Jacob : j’ai promis de donner ce pays à eux et à leurs descendants après eux.”

sw.L: Tazama, nimeiweka nchi mbele yenu; ingieni mkaimiliki nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwaapia baba zenu, Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo, kwamba atawapa wao na uzao wao baada yao.'
sw.B: Tazama, nimeiweka nchi mbele yenu. Ingieni mkaimiliki nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliapa kuwapa mababu zenu Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo, na wazao wao baada yao.'
sw.R: Tazama, nchi iko mbele yenu, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} ninawapa. Ingieni mkaichukue iwe yenu. Mimi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, niliwaahidi mababu zenu Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo kwa kiapo. Niliahidi kuwapa nchi hii wao na wazao wao baada yao.'

ko.L: 보아라, 내가 그 땅을 너희 앞에 두었다. 들어가서 그 땅을 차지하라. 그것은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희 조상들, 곧 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱에게, 그들과 그들 뒤의 자손에게 주겠다고 맹세하신 땅이다.'
ko.B: 보아라, 내가 그 땅을 너희 앞에 두었다. 들어가서 그 땅을 차지하라. 그 땅은 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 너희 조상 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱에게, 그리고 그들 뒤의 자손에게 주겠다고 맹세한 땅이다.'
ko.R: 보아라, 그 땅이 너희 앞에 있다. 내가 그 땅을 너희에게 준다. 들어가서 너희 것으로 차지하라. 나 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}는 너희 조상 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱에게 맹세하며 약속했다. 그 땅을 그들과 그들의 자손에게 주겠다고 약속했다.'

vi.L: Hãy xem, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đặt xứ ấy trước mặt các ngươi. Hãy đi vào và chiếm hữu xứ mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thề với cha ông các ngươi, với Áp-ra-ham, với Y-sác và với Gia-cốp, [là sẽ] ban [nó] cho họ và cho dòng dõi họ sau họ.'
vi.B: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã đặt xứ ấy trước mặt các ngươi. Hãy vào chiếm hữu xứ mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thề ban cho tổ tiên các ngươi là Áp-ra-ham, Y-sác và Gia-cốp, cùng dòng dõi họ sau này.'
vi.R: Này, xứ ấy ở ngay trước mặt các ngươi, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban nó cho các ngươi. Hãy vào chiếm lấy làm của mình. Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thề hứa với tổ tiên các ngươi là Áp-ra-ham, Y-sác và Gia-cốp. Ta đã hứa ban xứ này cho họ và cho dòng dõi họ sau này.'

decisions.choice: take possession of: take over the land and hold it as your own
decisions.reason: The verb means to take over property and hold it, as an heir does. It runs through Deuteronomy: Israel is to go in and take possession of the land God gives (verse 21; 4:1; 6:18). Used of nations, the same verb means to drive them out.

decisions.choice: the oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: God's sworn promise of the land
decisions.reason: God promised the land to Abraham and his offspring (Genesis 12:7; 15:18-21) and confirmed it with an oath (Genesis 22:16-17; 26:3; 50:24). Deuteronomy often recalls this oath as the ground of Israel's hope (6:10, 18; 7:8).

decisions.choice: the LORD swore: God speaks of himself by name
decisions.reason: The words are still God's, begun in verse 6, but God names himself in the third person, "the land that the LORD swore". This is a common way for God to speak of his own promises in the Old Testament; it does not mean that another speaker has taken over.

decisions.choice: See ... I have set: the land is as good as given
decisions.reason: "See" is addressed to the people as one (the Hebrew uses the singular), and the following verbs are plural. "I have set" is the language of a done deal: the land lies open, already given, and Israel has only to go in.

decisions.choice: I, the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that God is still speaking about himself, where Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew's "the LORD swore".

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "fathers", here meaning forefathers. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", the ordinary word for those who came before.

decisions.choice: "Mira" (singular), then plural forms ("entren y tomen posesión")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy: Moses (and God in his words) addresses Israel now as one, in the singular, and now as many, in the plural, often in the same sentence. Spanish follows the Hebrew number at every level: "tú" forms where the Hebrew is singular, with no setting, and plural forms under the plural-you setting where it is plural. Here "See" is singular (m4) and the following verbs are plural.

decisions.choice: "Vois", "Regarde" (singular), then "vous" (plural)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy: Moses (and God in his words) addresses Israel now as one, in the singular, and now as many, in the plural. French has the same two forms, so it follows the Hebrew number at every level, "tu" where the Hebrew is singular and "vous" where it is plural, even when the two meet in one sentence, as here (m4).

decisions.choice: "Tazama" (singular), then plural forms ("mbele yenu", "ingieni")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy: Moses (and God in his words) addresses Israel now as one, in the singular, and now as many, in the plural. Swahili has the same two forms (wewe, ninyi, and the verb prefixes u-, m-), so it follows the Hebrew number at every level, even when the two meet in one sentence, as here (m4). At Readable "nami" (and I) for God takes the deity pronoun span.

decisions.choice: God speaks of himself by name in the third person at Literal ("{Y}께서 ... 맹세하신"); Balanced and Readable say "나 {Y}"
decisions.reason: Korean honorific endings would make God honour himself in his own speech; Balanced and Readable avoid that by using the first person with the name, as the English Readable does. Literal keeps the Hebrew's third person.

decisions.choice: "chiếm hữu" (L, B); "chiếm lấy làm của mình" (R) for take possession
decisions.reason: The verb means to take over the land and hold it as one's own (meaning decision); "chiếm hữu" is the word of Numbers 21:24 and Joshua 1:11, used through the book. Readable spells it out in plain words.

decisions.choice: "cha ông" (L); "tổ tiên" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of fathers; Balanced and Readable say ancestors. Neither needs the gender setting in Vietnamese.

source.text: וָאֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵכֶ֔ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹא־אוּכַ֥ל לְבַדִּ֖י שְׂאֵ֥ת אֶתְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I said to you at the time the that, saying, Not I am able by myself to bear you.

en.L: And I said to you at that time, 'I am not able by myself to bear you.
en.B: Back then I told you, 'Carrying all of you on my own is more than I can do.
en.R: At that time I said to you, 'I cannot take care of all of you by myself.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:les|os}} dije en aquel tiempo: “No puedo yo solo {{plural_you:llevarlos|llevaros}}.
es.B: En aquel entonces {{plural_you:les|os}} dije: “Cargar con todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} yo solo es más de lo que puedo.
es.R: En aquel tiempo {{plural_you:les|os}} dije: “No puedo cuidar de todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} yo solo.

fr.L: Et je vous ai dit en ce temps-là : “Je ne peux pas, à moi seul, vous porter.
fr.B: À cette époque, je vous ai dit : “Vous porter tous, à moi seul, c’est au-dessus de mes forces.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, je vous ai dit : “Je ne peux pas m’occuper de vous tous tout seul.

sw.L: Nami niliwaambia wakati ule, nikisema, 'Siwezi peke yangu kuwachukua ninyi.
sw.B: Wakati ule niliwaambia, 'Kuwabeba ninyi nyote peke yangu ni zaidi ya uwezo wangu.
sw.R: Wakati huo niliwaambia, 'Siwezi kuwatunza ninyi nyote peke yangu.

ko.L: 그리고 그때에 내가 너희에게 말했다. '나 혼자서는 너희를 감당할 수 없다.
ko.B: 그때에 나는 너희에게 말했다. '나 혼자서 너희를 모두 짊어지기에는 힘에 부친다.
ko.R: 그때에 나는 여러분에게 말했습니다. '나 혼자서는 여러분을 모두 돌볼 수 없습니다.

vi.L: Và vào lúc ấy tôi đã nói với các ngươi rằng: 'Một mình tôi không thể gánh vác các ngươi.
vi.B: Hồi đó tôi đã nói với anh em: 'Một mình tôi không thể gánh vác hết thảy anh em được.
vi.R: Lúc ấy tôi đã nói với anh em: 'Tôi không thể một mình lo cho tất cả anh em.

decisions.choice: at that time I said: the appointment of leaders, told also in Exodus 18 and Numbers 11
decisions.reason: Exodus 18:13-26 tells how Moses, on the advice of his father-in-law Jethro, chose capable men to judge the people with him, and Numbers 11:14-17 how Moses said he could not carry the people alone and the LORD gave seventy elders to share the load. Moses here recalls these events in his own way, as his own proposal to the people, without naming Jethro. "At that time" is the time at Horeb, before the people set out.

decisions.choice: to bear you: to carry the load of leading the people
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift and carry. Here the load is the work of leading the people and settling their quarrels (verse 12), the same picture Moses uses in Numbers 11:11-14.

decisions.choice: Moses calls himself "나" in his 합쇼체 address at Readable, not the humble "저"
decisions.reason: Moses speaks as the people's leader and God's spokesman; "나" with 합쇼체 endings is the voice of a respected elder addressing an assembly, as Moses speaks to the people in the Korean Exodus.

decisions.choice: Moses to Israel: "tôi" for himself; "các ngươi" / "ngươi" (L), "anh em" (B, R) for the people
decisions.reason: The term sheet's rule for Moses' speeches. Literal keeps the Hebrew plural "các ngươi" and singular "ngươi" apart, as the English Literal keeps the plural and singular "you"; Balanced and Readable use "anh em", which a leader speaking to his own people says, for both.

source.text: יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם הִרְבָּ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֑ם וְהִנְּכֶ֣ם הַיּ֔וֹם כְּכוֹכְבֵ֥י הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם לָרֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh your God has multiplied you, and here you [are] today like [the] stars of the heavens for multitude.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has multiplied you, and here you [are] today like the stars of the heavens for multitude.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has increased your numbers, and look at you today: as many as the stars in the sky.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has made your people grow. Now there are as many of you as there are stars in the sky.

es.L: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:los|os}} ha multiplicado, y he aquí que hoy [{{plural_you:son|sois}}] como las estrellas de los cielos en multitud.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}} {{plural_you:los|os}} ha hecho crecer en número, y {{plural_you:mírense|miraos}} hoy: tantos como las estrellas del cielo.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{plural_you:su Dios ha hecho crecer a su pueblo|vuestro Dios ha hecho crecer a vuestro pueblo}}. Ahora {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}} tantos como las estrellas del cielo.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous a multipliés, et voici que vous [êtes] aujourd’hui comme les étoiles des cieux en nombre.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu vous a rendus nombreux : regardez-vous aujourd’hui, aussi nombreux que les étoiles du ciel !
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} votre Dieu a fait grandir votre peuple. Maintenant, vous êtes aussi nombreux que les étoiles dans le ciel.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu amewaongeza, na tazama, leo ninyi [ni] kama nyota za mbinguni kwa wingi.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu ameiongeza hesabu yenu, na jitazameni leo: mko wengi kama nyota za angani.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wenu amewafanya muongezeke. Sasa mko wengi kama nyota angani.

ko.L: 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희를 많게 하셨으니, 보아라, 오늘 너희는 수가 하늘의 별들과 같다.
ko.B: 너희 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희를 번성하게 하셨다. 보아라, 오늘 너희는 하늘의 별처럼 많다.
ko.R: 여러분의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여러분의 수를 늘리셨습니다. 이제 여러분은 하늘의 별처럼 많아졌습니다.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của các ngươi đã làm cho các ngươi gia tăng, và kìa, hôm nay các ngươi [đông] như sao trên trời về số lượng.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đã làm cho anh em gia tăng, và kìa, hôm nay anh em đông như sao trên trời.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của anh em đã làm cho anh em thêm đông đúc. Giờ đây số anh em nhiều như sao trên trời.

decisions.choice: like the stars of the heavens: the promise to Abraham fulfilled
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham that his offspring would be as many as the stars (Genesis 15:5; 22:17; 26:4). Moses says the promise has come true (10:22). His trouble is not that the people are too many; that is God's blessing. The trouble is that one man cannot lead so many.

decisions.choice: like the stars for multitude: very many, a picture and not a count
decisions.reason: The comparison is a way of saying "beyond counting", as in 10:22 and 28:62. It does not give a number.

source.text: יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבֽוֹתֵכֶ֗ם יֹסֵ֧ף עֲלֵיכֶ֛ם כָּכֶ֖ם אֶ֣לֶף פְּעָמִ֑ים וִיבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶתְכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh, [the] God of your fathers, may he add to you like you [are] a thousand times, and may he bless you just as he spoke to you.

en.L: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your fathers, add to you a thousand times as many as you [are], and bless you just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has spoken to you!
en.B: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, increase you a thousandfold beyond what you are now, and bless you as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised!
en.R: I pray that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}, will make you a thousand times more than you are now. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bless you, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised.

es.L: ¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} añada mil veces tanto como [{{plural_you:son|sois}}], y {{plural_you:los|os}} bendiga tal como {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dicho!
es.B: ¡Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}, {{plural_you:los|os}} multiplique mil veces más de lo que {{plural_you:son|sois}} ahora, y {{plural_you:los|os}} bendiga como {{plural_you:les|os}} prometió!
es.R: Oro para que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}}, {{plural_you:los|os}} haga mil veces más numerosos de lo que {{plural_you:son|sois}} ahora. Que {{plural_you:los|os}} bendiga, tal como {{plural_you:les|os}} prometió.

fr.L: Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de vos pères, vous ajoute mille fois autant que vous [êtes], et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous bénisse comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous l’a dit !
fr.B: Que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, vous rende mille fois plus nombreux que vous ne l’êtes, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous bénisse comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a promis !
fr.R: Je prie pour que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, le Dieu de vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, vous rende mille fois plus nombreux que maintenant. Qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous bénisse, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a promis.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa baba zenu, na awaongeze mara elfu kama mlivyo, na awabariki kama alivyowaambia!
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mababu zenu, na awazidishe mara elfu kuliko mlivyo sasa, na awabariki kama alivyoahidi!
sw.R: Ninaomba kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa mababu zenu, awafanye muwe wengi mara elfu kuliko mlivyo sasa. Na awabariki, kama alivyoahidi.

ko.L: 너희 조상들의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희를 지금 너희의 천 배나 더하시고, 너희에게 말씀하신 대로 너희에게 복을 주시기를 [바란다].
ko.B: 너희 조상들의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 너희를 지금보다 천 배나 더 많게 하시고, 약속하신 대로 너희에게 복을 주시기를 바란다.
ko.R: 여러분 조상들의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 여러분을 지금보다 천 배나 더 많게 해 주시기를 기도합니다. 그분께서 약속하신 대로 여러분에게 복을 주시기를 바랍니다.

vi.L: Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của cha ông các ngươi, làm cho các ngươi thêm gấp ngàn lần [số] các ngươi [hiện có], và ban phước cho các ngươi như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán với các ngươi!
vi.B: Nguyện {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của tổ tiên anh em, làm cho anh em gia tăng gấp ngàn lần số hiện nay, và ban phước cho anh em như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hứa!
vi.R: Tôi cầu xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của tổ tiên anh em, làm cho anh em đông gấp ngàn lần hiện nay. Nguyện {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban phước cho anh em như {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hứa.

decisions.choice: may he add ... may he bless: a wish and a prayer
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form of a wish. Moses breaks off to bless the people's growth, so that no one hears his words in verse 9 as a complaint about their numbers.

decisions.choice: a thousand times: far more, without limit
decisions.reason: "A thousand times" is a way of saying "many times over". It is not a calculation.

decisions.choice: as he spoke to you: as he promised
decisions.reason: "Speak" here means to promise, as when God told Abraham he would bless him and make him a great nation (Genesis 12:2; 22:17).

decisions.choice: I pray that
decisions.reason: Readable turns the wish into a plain prayer, which is what "may he" expresses.

decisions.choice: no deity pronoun span here ("{{plural_you:los|os}} bendiga tal como {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dicho"); spans only on written words (él/Él, lo/Lo, le/Le, su/Su, mí/Mí, me/Me, tú/Tú, te/Te, ti/Ti, tu/Tu)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy, as in Genesis and Exodus: the deity pronoun setting goes on the Spanish words for God that Spanish writes out. The English "he" here is only in the Spanish verb ending, so there is no span; Spanish does not add "él" just to carry the setting. The English "ancestors" gender span has no Spanish counterpart either: "antepasados" already includes women.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}; "vos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}" (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy, as in Genesis and Exodus: every pronoun for God takes the deity pronoun setting, lowercase by default and capitalised as the alternative (il, lui, le, l', son, sa, ses, and moi, me, mon, toi, te, tu, ton when God speaks or is spoken to). "Je" has no span, and a pronoun that opens a sentence is written plainly with its capital. The gender span on "ancêtres" / "pères" mirrors the English one.

decisions.choice: no deity pronoun span here ("kama alivyowaambia", "kama alivyoahidi")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy, as in Genesis and Exodus: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb, where no capital is possible, so the deity pronoun setting goes only on free pronouns for God (yeye, naye, mimi, nami, wewe, and the possessives wake, yake, wangu, yako...). The English "he" is the verb prefix here, so there is no span.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span: "그분" and the honorific "-시-" for God
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect for God is carried by "그분", "께서" and "-시-" at every level, as the Korean style guide sets. Recorded once for the book.

decisions.choice: "조상들" for "fathers", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "조상" already means ancestors without naming sex, so the English gender setting (ancestors / fathers) has no Korean pair to switch.

source.text: אֵיכָ֥ה אֶשָּׂ֖א לְבַדִּ֑י טָרְחֲכֶ֥ם וּמַֽשַּׂאֲכֶ֖ם וְרִֽיבְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: How will I bear by myself your trouble and your load and your strife?

en.L: How can I bear by myself your trouble and your load and your disputes?
en.B: How am I to carry on my own all your troubles, the load you put on me, and your quarrels?
en.R: How can I handle all your problems, your needs and your arguments by myself?

es.L: ¿Cómo llevaré yo solo {{plural_you:su molestia, su carga y sus pleitos|vuestra molestia, vuestra carga y vuestros pleitos}}?
es.B: ¿Cómo voy a cargar yo solo con todos {{plural_you:sus problemas|vuestros problemas}}, con el peso que {{plural_you:ponen|ponéis}} sobre mí y con {{plural_you:sus pleitos|vuestros pleitos}}?
es.R: ¿Cómo puedo resolver yo solo todos {{plural_you:sus problemas, sus necesidades y sus discusiones|vuestros problemas, vuestras necesidades y vuestras discusiones}}?

fr.L: Comment porterais-je à moi seul votre peine, votre charge et vos disputes ?
fr.B: Comment porterais-je seul tous vos soucis, le poids que vous faites peser sur moi et vos querelles ?
fr.R: Comment pourrais-je régler seul tous vos problèmes, vos besoins et vos disputes ?

sw.L: Nitawezaje kubeba peke yangu taabu yenu, na mzigo wenu, na mashindano yenu?
sw.B: Nitawezaje kubeba peke yangu shida zenu zote, mzigo mnaouweka juu yangu, na magomvi yenu?
sw.R: Ninawezaje kushughulikia peke yangu matatizo yenu yote, mahitaji yenu na mabishano yenu?

ko.L: 내가 어떻게 혼자서 너희의 짐과 너희의 무거운 짐과 너희의 다툼을 감당하겠느냐?
ko.B: 너희의 골칫거리와 너희가 지우는 짐과 너희의 다툼을 내가 어떻게 혼자 다 짊어지겠느냐?
ko.R: 여러분의 온갖 문제와 필요와 다툼을 내가 어떻게 혼자서 다 감당하겠습니까?

vi.L: Làm sao một mình tôi gánh nổi sự phiền nhọc của các ngươi, gánh nặng của các ngươi và sự tranh tụng của các ngươi?
vi.B: Làm sao một mình tôi gánh vác nổi mọi phiền toái của anh em, gánh nặng anh em đặt trên tôi, và những vụ tranh chấp của anh em?
vi.R: Làm sao một mình tôi có thể lo hết những khó khăn, nhu cầu và những cuộc cãi vã của anh em?

decisions.choice: trouble, load, strife: the weight of the people's needs and their quarrels
decisions.reason: Three words pile up the burden. The first means a heavy trouble (Isaiah 1:14 uses it for what God is weary of carrying); the second is a load to be carried; the third is a quarrel or lawsuit. The last points to the need for judges in verses 13-17.

decisions.choice: how can I bear: a question expecting the answer "I cannot"
decisions.reason: Moses does not ask for information; he is saying that the task is beyond one man (verse 9).

source.text: הָב֣וּ לָ֠כֶם אֲנָשִׁ֨ים חֲכָמִ֧ים וּנְבֹנִ֛ים וִידֻעִ֖ים לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶ֑ם וַאֲשִׂימֵ֖ם בְּרָאשֵׁיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Provide for yourselves men wise and understanding and known, from your tribes, and I will set them as your heads.

en.L: Provide for yourselves men [who are] wise and understanding and known, from your tribes, and I will set them as your heads.'
en.B: From your tribes, pick men who are wise, discerning and well known, and I will put them at your head.'
en.R: Each tribe should choose men who are wise and have good sense, men whom people know and trust. Then I will make them your leaders.'

es.L: {{plural_you:Provéanse|Proveeos}} de hombres sabios, entendidos y conocidos, de {{plural_you:sus tribus|vuestras tribus}}, y yo los pondré como {{plural_you:sus jefes|vuestros jefes}}.”
es.B: {{plural_you:Escojan|Escoged}} de entre {{plural_you:sus tribus|vuestras tribus}} hombres sabios, prudentes y respetados, y yo los pondré al frente de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.”
es.R: Que cada tribu escoja hombres sabios y con buen juicio, hombres que la gente conozca y en quienes confíe. Luego yo los nombraré {{plural_you:sus líderes|vuestros líderes}}.”

fr.L: Procurez-vous des hommes sages, intelligents et connus, [pris] dans vos tribus, et je les établirai comme vos chefs.”
fr.B: Choisissez dans vos tribus des hommes sages, avisés et reconnus, et je les mettrai à votre tête.”
fr.R: Que chaque tribu choisisse des hommes sages et pleins de bon sens, des hommes que les gens connaissent et en qui ils ont confiance. Ensuite, j’en ferai vos chefs.”

sw.L: Jipatieni watu wenye hekima, na ufahamu, na wanaojulikana, kutoka katika makabila yenu, nami nitawaweka kuwa wakuu wenu.'
sw.B: Chagueni kutoka katika makabila yenu watu wenye hekima, wenye busara na wanaoheshimika, nami nitawaweka wawe viongozi wenu.'
sw.R: Kila kabila liwachague watu wenye hekima na akili nzuri, watu ambao wengine wanawajua na kuwaamini. Kisha nitawafanya kuwa viongozi wenu.'

ko.L: 너희 지파들에서 지혜롭고 분별력 있고 알려진 사람들을 너희를 위하여 뽑아라. 그러면 내가 그들을 너희의 우두머리로 세우겠다.'
ko.B: 너희 각 지파에서 지혜롭고 분별력 있고 존경받는 사람들을 뽑아라. 그러면 내가 그들을 너희의 지도자로 세우겠다.'
ko.R: 각 지파에서 지혜롭고 판단력이 좋으며, 사람들이 잘 알고 믿을 만한 사람들을 뽑으십시오. 그러면 내가 그들을 여러분의 지도자로 세우겠습니다.'

vi.L: Hãy chọn cho các ngươi những người khôn ngoan, thông sáng và được biết đến, từ các chi tộc của các ngươi, và tôi sẽ lập họ làm đầu các ngươi.'
vi.B: Hãy chọn từ các chi tộc của anh em những người khôn ngoan, sáng suốt và có uy tín, rồi tôi sẽ lập họ đứng đầu anh em.'
vi.R: Mỗi chi tộc hãy chọn những người khôn ngoan và hiểu biết, là những người được mọi người biết đến và tin cậy. Rồi tôi sẽ lập họ làm người lãnh đạo anh em.'

decisions.choice: wise, understanding and known: men of practical wisdom and good judgment, known and respected in their tribes
decisions.reason: "Wise" is skill in living and in handling matters; "understanding" is the ability to see what is right in a case (1 Kings 3:9, 12). "Known" means that their tribes know them and their character: they are proven men, not strangers. Exodus 18:21 adds that the leaders must fear God, be trustworthy and hate bribes.

decisions.choice: provide for yourselves ... and I will set them: the people choose and Moses appoints
decisions.reason: The people are to put forward the men, and Moses gives them their office. In Exodus 18:25 Moses himself chooses them; here he stresses the people's share in the choice, as their agreement in verse 14 does.

decisions.choice: men whom people know and trust
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what it means to be "known" in a tribe: to have a name people can rely on.

decisions.choice: "tribu" for shevet; "clan" and "famille" kept for the smaller units
decisions.reason: For the whole of Deuteronomy, as the Pentateuch terms list: "la tribu", "el clan" / "le clan", "la famille" (Spanish "la tribu", Swahili "kabila", plural "makabila").

source.text: וַֽתַּעֲנ֖וּ אֹתִ֑י וַתֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ טֽוֹב־הַדָּבָ֥ר אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And you answered me and said, Good [is] the thing which you have spoken to do.

en.L: And you answered me and said, 'Good [is] the thing that you have spoken, to do [it].'
en.B: You answered me, 'Your plan is a good one; let it be done.'
en.R: You answered, 'That is a good plan. Let us do it.'

es.L: Y {{plural_you:me respondieron|me respondisteis}} y {{plural_you:dijeron|dijisteis}}: “Buena [es] la cosa que has dicho, para hacer[la].”
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes me respondieron|Vosotros me respondisteis}}: “Tu plan es bueno; que se lleve a cabo.”
es.R: {{plural_you:Me respondieron|Me respondisteis}}: “Es un buen plan. Hagámoslo.”

fr.L: Et vous m’avez répondu et vous avez dit : “Bonne [est] la chose que tu as dite, à faire.”
fr.B: Vous m’avez répondu : “Ton projet est bon, qu’il soit mis en œuvre !”
fr.R: Vous m’avez répondu : “C’est un bon plan. Faisons-le !”

sw.L: Nanyi mkanijibu na kusema, 'Ni jema neno ulilosema, kulifanya.'
sw.B: Nanyi mlinijibu, 'Mpango wako ni mzuri; na utekelezwe.'
sw.R: Mlinijibu, 'Huo ni mpango mzuri. Tuufanye.'

ko.L: 그러자 너희가 나에게 대답하여 말했다. '당신이 말씀하신 일은 하기에 좋습니다.'
ko.B: 너희는 나에게 대답했다. '당신의 계획이 좋습니다. 그렇게 합시다.'
ko.R: 여러분은 대답했습니다. '좋은 계획입니다. 그렇게 합시다.'

vi.L: Và các ngươi đã trả lời tôi và nói: 'Điều ông đã nói là tốt để làm.'
vi.B: Anh em đã trả lời tôi: 'Kế hoạch của ông thật tốt; xin cứ làm như vậy.'
vi.R: Anh em trả lời: 'Kế hoạch ấy hay lắm. Chúng tôi xin làm theo.'

decisions.choice: good to do: the people agree to the plan
decisions.reason: The people give their consent. Moses recalls it so that they remember the leaders were their own choice as well as his.

decisions.choice: plan
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the word" or "the thing" that Moses had spoken. Balanced and Readable call it a plan, which is what it was.

decisions.choice: "tú" for Moses ("has dicho", "tu plan") inside the people's plural answer
decisions.reason: The people speak to Moses as one person, and the Hebrew verb is singular, so Spanish uses "tú", as it does for every single person addressed; their own verbs are plural and take the plural-you setting.

decisions.choice: The people speak to Moses in 합쇼체 with "당신"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for the people speaking to Moses and Aaron; "당신" serves as a respectful second person in reported speech, with formal polite endings.

decisions.choice: The people to Moses: "ông", and "chúng tôi" for themselves
decisions.reason: The term sheet's address for the people speaking to Moses. Readable says "Chúng tôi xin làm theo" where the English Readable says "Let us do it": the people are agreeing to what Moses proposed.

source.text: וָאֶקַּ֞ח אֶת־רָאשֵׁ֣י שִׁבְטֵיכֶ֗ם אֲנָשִׁ֤ים חֲכָמִים֙ וִֽידֻעִ֔ים וָאֶתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛ם רָאשִׁ֖ים עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם שָׂרֵ֨י אֲלָפִ֜ים וְשָׂרֵ֣י מֵא֗וֹת וְשָׂרֵ֤י חֲמִשִּׁים֙ וְשָׂרֵ֣י עֲשָׂרֹ֔ת וְשֹׁטְרִ֖ים לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I took [the] heads of your tribes, men wise and known, and I set them [as] heads over you, officers of thousands and officers of hundreds and officers of fifties and officers of tens, and officials for your tribes.

en.L: So I took the heads of your tribes, men [who were] wise and known, and I made them heads over you, officers of thousands and officers of hundreds and officers of fifties and officers of tens, and officials for your tribes.
en.B: So I took the leading men of your tribes, wise and respected men, and set them over you as leaders: commanders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties and of tens, and officials for each of your tribes.
en.R: So I took the leaders of your tribes, men who were wise and well known, and put them in charge of you. Some led groups of a thousand people, some led a hundred, some fifty, and some ten. Others became officials for your tribes.

es.L: Y tomé a los jefes de {{plural_you:sus tribus|vuestras tribus}}, hombres sabios y conocidos, y los puse como jefes sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}: oficiales de millares, oficiales de centenas, oficiales de cincuenta y oficiales de diez, y funcionarios para {{plural_you:sus tribus|vuestras tribus}}.
es.B: Así que tomé a los hombres principales de {{plural_you:sus tribus|vuestras tribus}}, hombres sabios y respetados, y los puse al frente de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}: comandantes de mil, de cien, de cincuenta y de diez, y funcionarios para cada una de {{plural_you:sus tribus|vuestras tribus}}.
es.R: Entonces tomé a los líderes de {{plural_you:sus tribus|vuestras tribus}}, hombres sabios y bien conocidos, y los puse a cargo de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Unos dirigían grupos de mil personas, otros de cien, otros de cincuenta y otros de diez. Otros llegaron a ser funcionarios de {{plural_you:sus tribus|vuestras tribus}}.

fr.L: Et j’ai pris les chefs de vos tribus, des hommes sages et connus, et je les ai établis chefs sur vous, officiers de milliers, officiers de centaines, officiers de cinquantaines et officiers de dizaines, et préposés pour vos tribus.
fr.B: J’ai donc pris les principaux hommes de vos tribus, des hommes sages et respectés, et je les ai mis à votre tête : commandants de mille, de cent, de cinquante et de dix, et préposés pour chacune de vos tribus.
fr.R: J’ai donc pris les chefs de vos tribus, des hommes sages et bien connus, et je les ai mis à votre tête. Certains dirigeaient des groupes de mille personnes, d’autres de cent, de cinquante ou de dix. D’autres sont devenus des responsables pour vos tribus.

sw.L: Basi nikawatwaa wakuu wa makabila yenu, watu wenye hekima na wanaojulikana, nikawaweka kuwa wakuu juu yenu, wakuu wa maelfu, na wakuu wa mamia, na wakuu wa hamsini, na wakuu wa kumi, na wasimamizi kwa ajili ya makabila yenu.
sw.B: Basi niliwachukua watu mashuhuri wa makabila yenu, watu wenye hekima na wanaoheshimika, nikawaweka wawe viongozi wenu: makamanda wa maelfu, wa mamia, wa hamsini na wa kumi, na wasimamizi kwa kila kabila lenu.
sw.R: Basi niliwachukua viongozi wa makabila yenu, watu wenye hekima na wanaojulikana vizuri, nikawapa mamlaka juu yenu. Wengine waliongoza vikundi vya watu elfu moja, wengine mia moja, wengine hamsini na wengine kumi. Wengine wakawa maafisa wa makabila yenu.

ko.L: 그래서 내가 너희 지파의 우두머리들, 곧 지혜롭고 알려진 사람들을 데려다가 그들을 너희 위에 우두머리로 세웠다. 곧 천부장과 백부장과 오십부장과 십부장과 너희 지파의 관리들이다.
ko.B: 그래서 나는 너희 지파의 지도자들, 곧 지혜롭고 존경받는 사람들을 데려다가 너희를 다스리는 지도자로 세웠다. 그들은 천부장, 백부장, 오십부장, 십부장이 되었고, 너희 각 지파의 관리가 되었다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 여러분 지파의 지도자들, 곧 지혜롭고 잘 알려진 사람들을 데려다가 여러분을 맡아 이끌게 했습니다. 어떤 사람은 천 명을, 어떤 사람은 백 명을, 어떤 사람은 오십 명을, 어떤 사람은 열 명을 이끌었습니다. 또 어떤 사람들은 여러분 지파의 관리가 되었습니다.

vi.L: Vậy tôi đã lấy những người đứng đầu các chi tộc của các ngươi, những người khôn ngoan và được biết đến, và lập họ làm đầu trên các ngươi: trưởng ngàn người, trưởng trăm người, trưởng năm mươi người, trưởng mười người, và các viên chức cho các chi tộc của các ngươi.
vi.B: Vậy tôi chọn những người lãnh đạo trong các chi tộc của anh em, là những người khôn ngoan và có uy tín, và lập họ cai quản anh em: người chỉ huy nghìn người, trăm người, năm mươi người và mười người, cùng các viên chức cho từng chi tộc của anh em.
vi.R: Vậy tôi chọn những người lãnh đạo trong các chi tộc của anh em, là những người khôn ngoan và được nhiều người biết đến, và giao cho họ trông coi anh em. Có người coi một nhóm một nghìn người, có người coi một trăm, có người năm mươi, có người mười. Những người khác thì làm viên chức cho các chi tộc của anh em.

decisions.choice: officers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens: a ranked order of leaders
decisions.reason: The people are organized in groups of different sizes, each with its own leader, as in Exodus 18:21, 25. The same ranks are used for an army (Numbers 31:14, 48), and here they also serve to settle disputes (verses 16-17). How large a "thousand" was is discussed at Numbers 1.

decisions.choice: officials: men who kept records and carried out orders
decisions.reason: This word names officers who served under leaders and judges: the Israelite foremen in Egypt (Exodus 5:14-19), helpers of the elders (Numbers 11:16), and officers who gave orders to the army (20:5-9). Deuteronomy 16:18 sets them beside judges in every town.

decisions.choice: wise and known: the qualities asked for in verse 13
decisions.reason: Verse 15 names two of the three qualities in verse 13 and leaves out "understanding". The shorter list sums up the same request; it does not lower the standard.

decisions.choice: officers (Literal), commanders (Balanced), led (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for these leaders is used of princes, court officials and army captains. Here it names the leader of a group of a given size, so Literal says "officers", Balanced "commanders", and Readable says plainly what they did. Balanced keeps "officials" for the different word at the end of the verse.

decisions.choice: "préposés" for the shoterim (L, B); "responsables" (R)
decisions.reason: The shoterim kept records and carried out orders under the leaders (m2). "Scribes" would make them only writers, so French uses "préposés", officers put in charge of a task, as the English "officials", and keeps it apart from the "officiers" / "commandants" earlier in the verse.

decisions.choice: "wasimamizi" for the shoterim (L, B); "maafisa" (R)
decisions.reason: The shoterim kept records and carried out orders (m2), so Swahili calls them "wasimamizi" (overseers), keeping them apart from the "wakuu" / "makamanda" of the groups; Readable says "maafisa", the everyday word for officials.

decisions.choice: "천부장, 백부장, 오십부장, 십부장" for the officers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens
decisions.reason: These are the established Korean words for the ranked leaders; Readable says in plain words how many each led, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "trưởng" (L), "người chỉ huy" (B); "viên chức" for the officials
decisions.reason: The officers are a ranked order of leaders and the officials men who kept records and carried out orders (meaning decisions); "viên chức" covers both tasks without naming one.

source.text: וָאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶת־שֹׁ֣פְטֵיכֶ֔ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖וא לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁמֹ֤עַ בֵּין־אֲחֵיכֶם֙ וּשְׁפַטְתֶּ֣ם צֶ֔דֶק בֵּֽין־אִ֥ישׁ וּבֵין־אָחִ֖יו וּבֵ֥ין גֵּרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I commanded your judges at the time the that, saying, Hear between your brothers and judge righteously between a man and between his brother and between his sojourner.

en.L: And I commanded your judges at that time, saying, 'Hear [cases] between your brothers, and judge rightly between a man and his brother and the sojourner [who is] with him.
en.B: At that time I gave your judges this charge: 'Hear the disputes among your {{gender:fellow Israelites|brothers}}, and judge fairly in every case, whether it is between two Israelites or between an Israelite and a outsider living among you.
en.R: At that time I told your judges, 'Listen carefully to the arguments between your {{gender:fellow Israelites|brothers}}. Judge fairly, whether the case is between two Israelites or between an Israelite and a outsider who lives among you.

es.L: Y mandé a {{plural_you:sus jueces|vuestros jueces}} en aquel tiempo, diciendo: “{{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}} [las causas] entre {{plural_you:sus hermanos|vuestros hermanos}} y {{plural_you:juzguen|juzgad}} con justicia entre un hombre y su hermano y el extranjero [que está] con él.
es.B: En aquel tiempo di este encargo a {{plural_you:sus jueces|vuestros jueces}}: “{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} los pleitos entre {{plural_you:sus compatriotas|vuestros compatriotas}} y {{plural_you:juzguen|juzgad}} con imparcialidad en cada caso, sea entre dos israelitas o entre un israelita y un extranjero que vive entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: En aquel tiempo les dije a {{plural_you:sus jueces|vuestros jueces}}: “{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} con atención los pleitos entre {{plural_you:sus compatriotas|vuestros compatriotas}}. {{plural_you:Juzguen|Juzgad}} con justicia, tanto si el caso es entre dos israelitas como entre un israelita y un extranjero que vive entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Et j’ai donné ordre à vos juges en ce temps-là, en disant : “Écoutez [les causes] entre vos frères, et jugez avec justice entre un homme et son frère et l’étranger [qui est] avec lui.
fr.B: En ce temps-là, j’ai donné cette consigne à vos juges : “Écoutez les différends entre vos {{gender:compatriotes|frères}}, et jugez avec équité dans chaque affaire, qu’elle oppose deux Israélites ou un Israélite et un étranger qui vit parmi vous.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, j’ai dit à vos juges : “Écoutez bien les disputes entre vos {{gender:compatriotes|frères}}. Jugez de façon juste, que l’affaire oppose deux Israélites ou un Israélite et un étranger qui vit parmi vous.

sw.L: Nami nikawaamuru waamuzi wenu wakati ule, nikisema, 'Sikilizeni [mashauri] kati ya ndugu zenu, mkahukumu kwa haki kati ya mtu na ndugu yake na mgeni [aliye] pamoja naye.
sw.B: Wakati ule niliwapa waamuzi wenu agizo hili: 'Sikilizeni mashauri kati ya ndugu zenu Waisraeli, mkahukumu kwa haki katika kila shauri, liwe kati ya Waisraeli wawili au kati ya Mwisraeli na mgeni anayeishi kati yenu.
sw.R: Wakati huo niliwaambia waamuzi wenu, 'Sikilizeni kwa makini mabishano kati ya ndugu zenu Waisraeli. Hukumuni kwa haki, shauri likiwa kati ya Waisraeli wawili au kati ya Mwisraeli na mgeni anayeishi kati yenu.

ko.L: 그리고 그때에 내가 너희 재판관들에게 명령하여 말했다. '너희 형제들 사이의 [송사를] 듣고, 사람과 그의 형제 사이에서, 그리고 그와 함께 있는 나그네 사이에서 의롭게 재판하라.
ko.B: 그때에 나는 너희 재판관들에게 이렇게 일렀다. '너희 {{gender:동족|형제}} 사이의 송사를 잘 듣고 공정하게 재판하라. 이스라엘 사람끼리의 일이든, 이스라엘 사람과 너희 가운데 사는 나그네 사이의 일이든 마찬가지다.
ko.R: 그때에 나는 여러분의 재판관들에게 말했습니다. '{{gender:동족|형제}}끼리 다투는 말을 잘 들으십시오. 이스라엘 사람끼리의 일이든, 이스라엘 사람과 여러분 가운데 사는 나그네 사이의 일이든 공정하게 재판하십시오.

vi.L: Và vào lúc ấy tôi đã truyền cho các thẩm phán của các ngươi rằng: 'Hãy nghe [việc tranh tụng] giữa anh em các ngươi, và hãy xét xử công minh giữa một người với anh em mình và với ngoại kiều ở với người ấy.
vi.B: Lúc ấy tôi đã căn dặn các thẩm phán của anh em: 'Hãy nghe các vụ tranh chấp giữa những người đồng bào của anh em và xét xử công minh, dù là giữa hai người Y-sơ-ra-ên hay giữa một người Y-sơ-ra-ên với một ngoại kiều sống giữa anh em.
vi.R: Lúc ấy tôi đã dặn các thẩm phán của anh em: 'Hãy lắng nghe kỹ những vụ tranh cãi giữa đồng bào mình. Hãy xét xử công bằng, dù vụ việc là giữa hai người Y-sơ-ra-ên hay giữa một người Y-sơ-ra-ên với một người nước ngoài sống giữa anh em.

decisions.choice: hear between your brothers: hear both sides of a dispute
decisions.reason: To "hear between" two people is to listen to each party in a case before deciding it.

decisions.choice: brothers: fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: "Brother" here means a member of the same people, not a family member, as often in Deuteronomy (15:7; 17:15; 24:14). Disputes were brought by women as well as men (Numbers 27:1-5).

decisions.choice: righteously: by what is right, fairly and truly
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for what is right and just. A judgment is "righteous" when it gives each party what is right in God's eyes, without favor or bribe (16:18-20).

decisions.choice: the sojourner: a foreigner living in Israel
decisions.reason: The word names someone from outside who lives among a people without land or family there. Such people were easily wronged, and the law protects them again and again (10:18-19; 24:17; 27:19; Exodus 22:20). In court they are to get the same justice as an Israelite.

decisions.choice: between two Israelites or between an Israelite and an outsider
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "between a man and his brother and his sojourner". Balanced and Readable say what the two kinds of case are, which also lets them speak of any person rather than only of men.

decisions.choice: "compatriotas" (B, R), with no gender span; "el extranjero" for the ger
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "compatriotas" for the brothers, as the English says "fellow Israelites" (m2); like "hermanos", it already takes in women, so Spanish has no second wording for the gender setting. The ger is "el extranjero" throughout the Pentateuch, as the terms list sets.

decisions.choice: vos {{gender:compatriotes|frères}} (B, R); "l’étranger" for the ger
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced and Readable say who the brothers are, fellow members of the people, women included (m2), with the traditional "frères" under the gender setting; Literal keeps "frères". The ger is "l'étranger" throughout the Pentateuch, as the terms list sets.

decisions.choice: "ndugu zenu Waisraeli" (B, R), with no gender span; "mgeni" for the ger
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender span; Balanced and Readable add "Waisraeli" to say that fellow members of the people are meant, as the English "fellow Israelites". The ger is "mgeni" throughout the Pentateuch.

decisions.choice: {{gender:동족|형제}} for "brothers" meaning fellow Israelites; Literal keeps "형제들"
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span here (fellow Israelites / brothers); Korean has the same two ways of saying it, "동족" (one's own people) and "형제" (brothers). "형제자매" would suggest a family rather than the nation.

decisions.choice: Moses' charge to the judges at Readable is in 합쇼체, as it is part of his address to the whole people
decisions.reason: The words to the judges are recalled within Moses' speech to Israel; Readable keeps one speech level for the whole address.

decisions.choice: "anh em" (L), "đồng bào" (B, R) for brothers; "ngoại kiều" (L, B), "người nước ngoài sống giữa anh em" (R) for the sojourner
decisions.reason: Brothers here are fellow Israelites (meaning decision): Balanced and Readable say "đồng bào", which includes women and men, so no gender span is needed. "ngoại kiều" is the term sheet's word for the ger; Readable says what it means.
